newsitem.title: USA: IBM still faces tough Q1 comparison - Merrill.
newsitem.headline: IBM still faces tough Q1 comparison - Merrill.

text.p: Merrill Lynch analyst Daniel Mandresh said he expects International Business Machines Corp's first quarter to remain a tough comparison with the year-ago period and he maintains an estimate of $2.32 a share.
"Our Q1 estimate for IBM calls for revenue growth of three percent and EPS of $2.32 vs $2.21, the narrowest gain of the year at five percent," Mandresh said in a report to clients.

Last month Mandresh lowered his first quarter earnings estimate on IBM due to the strengthening dollar outside the U.S. He expects a currency hit of about $0.20 a share, which would neutralize a $0.16-a-share benefit from a share buyback.
Mandresh reiterated his short-term and long-term buy ratings on IBM, saying he does not believe the company's fundamental outlook has changed.

"Our belief that a 13 P/E (price/earnings ratio) on our 1998 outlook of $15 (a share) is an appropriate goal," Mandresh said. "As the year progresses, both the currency and product comparison hurdles moderate quite a bit."
He said his full-year forecast for 1997 is still revenues of $80.5 billion, up six percent from 1996, and earnings of $12.50 a share, up 13 percent.
